newsitem.title: UK: Euro life insurers defend sales channels - report.
newsitem.headline: Euro life insurers defend sales channels - report.

text.p: Most European life and pensions companies believe that they should not abandon their traditional intermediary channels, despite growing pressure on margins, a Datamonitor report said on Monday.

"Although Datamonitor predicts there will be a reduction in the number of intermediaries in most European life and pensions markets, intermediaries and company employees are still predicted to dominate distribution in the year 2000," it said.
Management consultancy Datamonitor based its findings on a survey of leading European insurers.

Instead, insurers will strive to achieve better performance from their existing distribution channels, as most realise that changing their primary sales channel is often not feasible, added the report, "European Life Insurance and Pensions Distribution."
"They (insurers) would have to rely on traditional channels during a transition period, and intermediaries in France and the Netherlands have already shown an unwillingness to cooperate.

"Insurers are increasingly aware that closer intermediary management will be a crucial element in the insurance culture of the future, particularly since banks have emerged as low cost competitors," Datamonitor said.
Supporting and training intermediaries will lead to an increase in the amount spent on new technology, as will improving information flows.
